ov: Thirty-six species of venomous pit vipers of the Americas, named for the rattle of interlocking keratin segments at the tail tip. They rarely bite unless provoked.

why.dg: Rattlesnakes cause the most snakebites in North America, but they rarely bite unless provoked, and treated bites are seldom fatal.
why.h: Rattlesnakes brumate through winter, sometimes over 1,000 of them huddled together in underground dens.
why.ac: Its eyes and heat-sensing pits help it hunt warm-blooded prey at night.
why.et: Eaten in places, and said to taste "just like chicken".

rg: The Americas, from southern Canada to central Argentina.
df: Small animals such as rodents and birds.
fx: Heat-sensing pits on its face let it “see” warm prey in the dark.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is confirmed: a new segment is added each time the snake sheds, several times a year. REGION: the range runs through Central America too; consider adding it. No why.et: the source doesn’t mention eating rattlesnakes. RESOLVED (owner: approve all): Central America added to r.
